best_for: Small publishers, clubs and designers who lay out flyers, newsletters or books for print and want CMYK and PDF output without paying for InDesign.

points.title: Made for print
points.text: Scribus handles CMYK and spot colors, ICC color management, color separations and PDF creation for press-ready output, plus EPS import and export.

points.title: Many scripts and languages
points.text: Its text engine handles right-to-left scripts such as Arabic and Hebrew, bidirectional text, Indic scripts and OpenType features, with support for more than 500 languages.

points.title: Free under the GPL
points.text: Scribus is open source and costs nothing, for personal or business use.

points.title: Versions differ by platform
points.text: The newest release, 1.6.7, came out in October 2026. On this site macOS has it, while the Windows listing tops out at 1.6.6 and the Flatpak at 1.6.5.

points.title: Linux: Flatpak is community-built
points.text: Flathub says its package is not verified by or affiliated with the Scribus developers. The project itself publishes an x86_64 AppImage.

points.title: Install details
points.text: Windows installers come in 32-bit and 64-bit and install for all users. Macs need macOS 13 or later, with separate Intel and Apple silicon disk images.

points.title: Downgrades
points.text: The Windows listing keeps 8 versions; macOS and Linux list only the current release, so downgrades there need another source. Older builds stay in the project's SourceForge archive.
